shortDescription: Allows certain items to be stacked beyond their normal stack size.
oneLiner: Raises the maximum stack size of items that vanilla keeps small or unstackable - potions, splash and lingering potions and tipped arrows stack to 64 by default, and so do stews, soups, ender pearls, eggs and a configurable list of items from other mods (eleven Tough As Nails entries plus Create's Builder's Tea ship in the default list).

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Eleven Tough As Nails items ship in the default stackable_items list - dirty_water_bottle, purified_water_bottle, seven juices (apple, cactus, chorus_fruit, glow_berry, melon, pumpkin, sweet_berry), ice_cream and charc_os - and are patched to a max stack of 64. Without Tough As Nails those entries simply find no item in the registry and are skipped (a WARN that is only printed with debug_logging on); nothing breaks, you just lose those eleven patches. Two caveats: filled canteens carry durability and can never be stacked, and the auto-detection of further TAN items that the README advertises does not run - the code is commented out. The ids themselves are marked as guessed in the source and are not verifiable in this repo.

configKeys.defaultValue: StackablesConfig.DEFAULT_STACKABLES (18 entries) = minecraft:mushroom_stew:64, minecraft:rabbit_stew:64, minecraft:beetroot_soup:64, minecraft:suspicious_stew:64, minecraft:ender_pearl:64, minecraft:egg:64, toughasnails:dirty_water_bottle:64, toughasnails:purified_water_bottle:64, toughasnails:apple_juice:64, toughasnails:cactus_juice:64, toughasnails:chorus_fruit_juice:64, toughasnails:glow_berry_juice:64, toughasnails:melon_juice:64, toughasnails:pumpkin_juice:64, toughasnails:sweet_berry_juice:64, toughasnails:ice_cream:64, toughasnails:charc_os:64, create:builders_tea:64
configKeys.range: per entry: at least two colons (the part before the last colon must itself contain a colon) and a stack part parsing to 1 ~ 64
configKeys.effect: List of item entries to make stackable, each in the format namespace:id:stack (e.g. minecraft:mushroom_stew:64); the last part is the desired max stack size. Ids that are not present in the item registry are skipped (WARN only with debug_logging on), malformed entries are skipped without any log. The runtime parser is looser than the config validator (see notes 10).

Default stack size for potions, splash potions, lingering potions and tipped arrows. Effective value is max(2, this) - setting 1 still yields 2, so vanilla's unstackable potions cannot be restored through this key (StackablesModule.java:73). The default was 16 until v0.9.3 (commit 73e2ffe).

notes:
SOURCE FOOTPRINT (find + grep over the whole repo, build/ excluded): modules/stackables/StackablesModule.java (239 lines), modules/stackables/config/StackablesConfig.java (109 lines), modules/stackables/constant_items/{StackablePotionItem,StackableSplashPotionItem,StackableLingeringPotionItem,StackableTippedArrowItem}.java, standalone/stackables/StackablesStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_stackables") -> StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot). There is NO mixin/stackables/ package and no stackables entry in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json. A grep for DeferredRegister / KeyMapping / RegisterCommandsEvent / RecipeManager / AddReloadListenerEvent / LootTableLoadEvent / ModList / shouldInitialize / isEnabledByDefault / Dist. / Minecraft.getInstance over the module returns ZERO hits: no registries, items, blocks, entities, commands, keybinds, recipes, no mod gate and no enabled-by-default override (Module.java:73 default true applies). No lang keys either - grep -i "stackab" in src/main/resources/assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/*.json returns nothing.

1) WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS. Everything happens in one handler, onModifyDefaultComponents(ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent) at EventPriority.LOWEST (StackablesModule.java:61-238), gated on isModuleEnabled() (:63). It (a) sets DataComponents.MAX_STACK_SIZE on Items.POTION, SPLASH_POTION, LINGERING_POTION and TIPPED_ARROW to max(2, default_potion_stack_size) (:73-81, whole block wrapped in try/catch Throwable -> warn), and (b) walks the stackable_items config list, splits each entry at the LAST colon, parses the ResourceLocation and the int, and patches MAX_STACK_SIZE for every id that resolves in BuiltInRegistries.ITEM (:97-147). Nothing else. Registration: onInitialize does getModEventBus().register(this) and falls back to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS with a warn if the mod bus is unavailable (:36-45) - both handlers are mod-bus events, so on that fallback path the module would silently do nothing (that ModifyDefaultComponentsEvent is a mod-bus event is NeoForge behaviour, not provable inside this repo).

2) DEAD CODE (three separate pieces). (a) The whole package modules/stackables/constant_items/ - StackablePotionItem, StackableSplashPotionItem, StackableLingeringPotionItem, StackableTippedArrowItem - is referenced NOWHERE in the repo (grep over *.java/*.json/*.gradle/*.toml/*.md finds only the files' own package/class/constructor lines). They are never registered and never instantiated. Three of them call new Item.Properties().stacksTo(16) in their constructor, the tipped arrow one stacksTo(64); they are the only place where "16" still exists and are almost certainly the origin of the README's "default 16". (b) onRegisterItems(RegisterEvent) (:55-59) is an empty @SubscribeEvent handler whose own comment says "This event is NOT used anymore" / "Keeping this method for potential future use". (c) StackablesModule.java:153 (a // TESTING: Disable auto-detection, only use config line) plus the block comment at :154-237 hold the entire Tough As Nails auto-detection. The commented text is itself syntactically broken ("int p" / newline / "atchedCount = 0;"), so it cannot simply be uncommented. Consequence: there is NO auto-detection at runtime - only the explicit stackable_items list is applied. Also commented out: the handledByConfig set at :91 and :119.

3) README CONTRADICTIONS (README.md:108-112, the "Stackables" paragraph). (a) "Potions / splash / lingering (default 16)" is stale: the live default is default_potion_stack_size = 64 and tipped arrows get the same value. Git proves the drift - 955f326 (2025-11-02) introduced the key with default 16, 73e2ffe (2026-05-08, "Bump version to 0.9.3 and increase potion stack size to 64") changed it to 64; the README bullet was never updated. (b) "Auto-detects Tough As Nails items (juices, water bottles, ice cream, empty canteens, ...)" is wrong - the auto-detection is commented out (see 2c). It was live only in v0.4.0 and has been dead since da0c512 (2025-11-02, first tag v0.4.1). TAN juices / water bottles / ice_cream / charc_os are covered only because they are hardcoded in DEFAULT_STACKABLES. (c) "empty canteens" are not covered at all: the path.startsWith("empty_") rule exists only inside the commented-out block and no toughasnails:empty_* entry is in DEFAULT_STACKABLES. (d) README.md:239 (optional-mods table) lists only Tough As Nails for this module and says "Only vanilla items are made stackable" without it - it omits Create, although create:builders_tea:64 ships in the default list.

4) MISLEADING LOG. With debug logging on, the module still prints "=== Starting auto-detection for Tough as Nails items ===" (:150-152) immediately before the dead block, so the log announces work that never happens. The matching "=== STACKABLES MODULE: Component patching complete ===" line sits inside the comment (:235-237) and is therefore never printed - a debug run ends after the per-item lines with no completion marker.

5) FLOOR OF 2. int desired = Math.max(2, getConfig().getDefaultPotionStackSize()); (:73). The config range allows 1, but setting 1 still yields a potion/tipped-arrow stack size of 2 - vanilla's unstackable potions cannot be restored through this key (only by disabling the module).

6) DURABILITY. Items that carry durability cannot also have MAX_STACK_SIZE > 1 in Minecraft, which is why filled TAN canteens stay unstackable (the README note is correct on that point). What this REPO proves is only the handling: event.modify is wrapped in try/catch Throwable and a failure is logged as "x Failed to patch {}: {}" at ERROR (:139-141), and the dead auto-detect block contains the author's own durability handling (skip when currentMax == 1, catch a message containing "durability", :191-197 / :216-220). That event.modify actually throws for a damageable item is NeoForge/vanilla behaviour and is not provable from this repository.

7) NO ModList GATE, AND SILENT FAILURE MODES. The module never calls ModList.isLoaded and never overrides shouldInitialize - missing mods are handled purely by BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.getOptional(...) coming back empty (:121), which logs "Item not found in registry" at WARN but only when debug_logging is on (:143-145). Malformed config entries are dropped with NO log at all: no colon or a trailing colon -> continue (:98-101), non-numeric stack part -> continue (:106-110), unparseable ResourceLocation -> continue (:112-117). The bundle's src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml does declare create (:82-88) and toughasnails (:90-96) as type="optional", but those are bundle-wide entries, not this module's doing; the generated standalone toml for vpa_stackables declares only vpa_core/neoforge/minecraft (required) plus vanillaplusadditions (incompatible) - build.gradle:507-513.

8) ID UNCERTAINTY IN SOURCE. StackablesConfig.java:51 carries the comment "NOTE: The toughasnails item IDs below are assumed/guessed; please verify actual IDs in your mod if necessary." Nothing in the repo verifies the eleven toughasnails ids or create:builders_tea (Tough As Nails and Create are compileOnly/absent here, the jars are not in the tree).

9) UNCONDITIONAL INFO LOG. StackablesConfig.onConfigLoad (:42-46) logs "StackablesConfig loaded - potion stack size: {}, stackable items count: {}" at INFO with no shouldDebugLog() gate - the rest of the module gates almost every log line. Both getters also fall back to the hardcoded defaults (DEFAULT_STACKABLES / 64) when the ConfigValue is null or throws, with a debug-level note (:85-108).

10) VALIDATOR vs PARSER MISMATCH. The defineList validator (:57-78) requires a String whose last colon is neither at index 0 nor at the end, whose resource part itself contains a further colon (so at least TWO colons overall - "a:b:c:64" passes as well, the module would then try to parse "a:b:c" as a ResourceLocation), and whose stack part parses to 1 <= v <= 64. The runtime parser (:97-117) is looser: one colon is enough and any int is accepted, so a hand-written "minecraft:egg:0" or "minecraft:egg:999" would be honoured by the parser but is rejected by the spec first. What NeoForge does with a rejected element (drop it or reset the whole list to the default) is not visible in this repository.

11) STANDALONE JAR. build.gradle:454 [ moduleId: 'stackables', displayName: 'Vanilla Plus: Stackables' ] - no mixins, no clientMixins, no dataGlobs, no moduleDeps beyond the implicit required vpa_core / neoforge / minecraft (build.gradle:508-513). The @Mod entrypoint standalone/stackables/StackablesStandalone.java exists, so the jar really boots the module. Bundle registration: VanillaPlusAdditions.java:160 moduleManager.registerModule(new StackablesModule()).

12) VERSION BOOKKEEPING (re-verified with git). ad1a391 (2025-11-01, "#MVA-2-Stackables ...") added StackablesModule + StackablesConfig; first tag containing it is v0.4.0 (CHANGELOG.md:1400-1402 documents it under [0.4.0] - 2025-11-02). 955f326 (same tag v0.4.0) added potions/tipped arrows + the TAN auto-detection; da0c512 (2025-11-02, first tag v0.4.1, CHANGELOG.md:1396-1398) commented the auto-detection out again. Later CHANGELOG touches: [0.7.1] line 1370 (more stackable items), [0.9.3] line 1340 (potion default 16 -> 64, commit 73e2ffe). The standalone jar came with the repo-wide roll-out 27c7405 (2026-07-01, beta.23).

13) NO DEDICATED DOC PAGE. There is no docs/modules/stackables.md - checked in the current working tree including the in-flight docs/ reorganisation (docs/modules/ holds 18 files, none for this module; find docs -iname '*stack*' is empty). README.md:108-112 plus the table row at :239 are the only prose that exists.

14) MULTIPLAYER (INFERRED, NOT PROVABLE HERE). MAX_STACK_SIZE is patched as a default data component during mod loading, so client and server each apply their own config; a mismatch would mean the two sides disagree about stack sizes. The repo contains no sync code, no config-sync annotation and no warning about this - the consequence is inferred from the mechanism, not stated anywhere in the source.
